title.suggested: St. Louis Sporting Men Discuss Allen's Challenge to Sullivan

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen's challenge to John L. Sullivan set the St. Louis fancy gossiping; Tom Kelly, Billy Carroll and Jack Looney judged Allen the better boxer but younger, heavier Sullivan the favorite.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, November 1, 1882

facts.fact: Tom Kelly said he thought Allen was born in 1840, making him 42
Allen and Bill Ryall came to St. Louis with a letter of introduction from Frank Queen to Jack Looney and Billy Carroll
Billy Carroll said Allen had left St. Louis a few years earlier and sailed for England, where he had been dissipating
Carroll said Allen easily defeated every man he met in America except Mace, who beat him

notes: Tom Kelly seconded both Allen and McCoole in fights near St. Louis.
